unc_qte

Source: R/unc_qte.R
unc_qte.Rd

Estimates the Quantile Treatment Effect (QTE) or Quantile Treatment Effect on the Treated (QTT) under unconfoundedness, also known as selection on observables, with cross-sectional data. The key identifying assumption is \((Y(0), Y(1)) \perp D \mid X\), i.e., potential outcomes are independent of treatment conditional on covariates \(X\). For staggered treatment adoption with panel or repeated cross-section data, see lou_qtt.

Three estimation methods are available via est_method:

"ipw"

Propensity-score reweighting (Firpo 2007). The propensity score \(p(X) = P(D=1|X)\) is estimated by logit or probit and used to reweight the sample so that the covariate distributions of the treated and untreated groups match. For the QTE, both groups are reweighted toward the population distribution; for the QTT, only the untreated group is reweighted toward the treated covariate distribution.

"reg"

Outcome regression via quantile regression inversion. rq is fit on a dense internal grid of \(\tau\) values, yielding a conditional quantile function \(Q_{Y|X,D=j}(\tau)\) for each arm \(j\). The marginal distribution is recovered by averaging conditional quantile functions over the empirical covariate distribution (Melly 2006; Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Melly 2013).

"aipw"

Doubly-robust augmented IPW. Combines the propensity score model with the conditional quantile outcome model. The CDF estimator is consistent if either the propensity score or the outcome model is correctly specified (semiparametric efficiency when both are correct).

When xformula = ~1 (the default), all three methods reduce to simple quantile differences between the treated and untreated groups, which is consistent under unconditional unconfoundedness. Covariates are required for covariate-adjusted estimation.

Rows with a missing value in the outcome, treatment, weights or any covariate in xformula are dropped, with a warning.

Standard errors and confidence intervals are computed via the empirical bootstrap, resampling rows of data, or whole clusters when clustervars is given.

Usage

unc_qte(
  yname,
  dname,
  data,
  xformula = ~1,
  weightsname = NULL,
  clustervars = NULL,
  probs = seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05),
  alp = 0.05,
  biters = 100,
  cband = TRUE,
  boot_type = "empirical",
  method = c("logit", "probit"),
  est_method = c("ipw", "reg", "aipw"),
  target = c("qte", "qtt"),
  cond_dist = c("qr", "dr"),
  cl = 1,
  xformla = NULL
)

Arguments

yname

character; name of the outcome variable in data.

dname

character; name of the binary treatment indicator in data (1 = treated, 0 = untreated).

data

data.frame containing the analysis data.

xformula

one-sided formula for covariates used in the propensity score and/or outcome model, e.g. ~ age + I(age^2) + education. Default ~1 uses no covariates (simple quantile differences).

weightsname

character; name of a column in data containing sampling weights. Default NULL applies equal weights.

clustervars

character; name of a column in data to cluster standard errors on (one variable). The bootstrap then resamples whole clusters instead of rows. Default NULL treats rows as independent.

probs

numeric vector of quantile levels at which to evaluate the QTE or QTT. Default seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05).

alp

significance level for confidence intervals. Default 0.05.

biters

number of bootstrap iterations for standard errors and confidence bands. Default 100.

cband

logical; if TRUE (default), qte.lower and qte.upper form a uniform confidence band, simultaneous over all quantiles in probs: qte \(\pm\) c \(\times\) qte.se, with the bootstrap critical value c computed from draws standardized by qte.se (as the panel estimators' uniform bands are). If FALSE, they are pointwise intervals, qte \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) qte.se.

boot_type

bootstrap variant. Currently only "empirical" is supported.

method

propensity score link function: "logit" (default) or "probit". Used by est_method = "ipw" and "aipw".

est_method

estimation method; one of:

  • "ipw" (default) — inverse propensity weighting

  • "reg" — outcome regression via quantile regression inversion ("or" is a deprecated alias)

  • "aipw" — doubly-robust augmented IPW

target

target parameter; one of:

  • "qte" (default) — population QTE: \(Q_{Y(1)}(\tau) - Q_{Y(0)}(\tau)\)

  • "qtt" — QTT (effect on the treated): \(Q_{Y(1)|D=1}(\tau) - Q_{Y(0)|D=1}(\tau)\)

cond_dist

For est_method = "reg" or "aipw", how the conditional outcome distributions are estimated: "qr" (default) for quantile regression or "dr" for distribution regression (a logit of \(1\{Y \le y\}\) on the covariates at a grid of thresholds; Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val and Melly 2013). Ignored for "ipw".

cl

number of cores for parallel bootstrap. Default 1 (sequential).

xformla

Deprecated; use xformula. Still accepted, with a warning.

Value

An object of class QTE containing:

qte

numeric vector of estimated QTE (or QTT) at each element of probs.

ate

estimated ATE (or ATT when target = "qtt").

qte.se

bootstrap standard errors for qte (the standard deviation of the bootstrap draws).

qte.lower, qte.upper

confidence bounds for qte: a uniform band if cband = TRUE, pointwise intervals otherwise (see cband).

cband

whether qte.lower/qte.upper are a uniform band.

ate.se, ate.lower, ate.upper

SE and CI for ate.

c

bootstrap critical value for a uniform band over probs.

probs

the probs vector passed by the user.

pscore.reg

fitted propensity score glm object (without copies of the data: coef(), vcov(), summary(), fitted() and predict(newdata = ) work; anova() and update() do not), or NULL when est_method = "reg".

F.treated.t, F.treated.t.cf

ECDFs of the estimated quantiles of \(Y(1)\) and \(Y(0)\) at probs.

Use summary() to print a formatted table and plot() to display the QTE curve with confidence bands.

Discrete outcomes

Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome. With mass points (e.g. many zeros) or few distinct values, quantiles jump and effects at quantiles inside a mass point are 0 by construction; identification based on ranks or quantile functions (change-in-changes, quantile DiD, the panel and distributional DiD copula arguments) only bounds the effects (Athey and Imbens 2006, Section 4); and bootstrap inference for quantiles can be unreliable. The estimators warn (once per call, class qte_discrete_outcome) when more than 10\ outcome's observations share one value or it takes at most 20 distinct values, across all groups and periods; the thresholds are the options qte.mass_point_tol and qte.discrete_n_unique. The diagnostics are returned as outcome_discreteness. cdf_did is identified for discrete outcomes.

References

Firpo, Sergio. “Efficient Semiparametric Estimation of Quantile Treatment Effects.” Econometrica 75(1), pp. 259–276, 2007.

Melly, Blaise. “Estimation of Counterfactual Distributions Using Quantile Regression.” Working paper, University of St. Gallen, 2006.

Chernozhukov, Victor, Ivan Fernandez-Val, and Blaise Melly. “Inference on Counterfactual Distributions.” Econometrica 81(6), pp. 2205–2268, 2013.

Examples

data(lalonde)

## IPW, no covariates (simple quantile differences)
# \donttest{
q1 <- unc_qte(yname = "re78", dname = "treat", data = lalonde.psid,
              biters = 20, probs = seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05))
#> Warning: The outcome `re78` looks discrete: 12% of observations equal 0. Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome. With mass points, quantiles jump and effects at quantiles inside a mass point are 0 by construction; rank- and quantile-based identification (e.g. change-in-changes) then only bounds the effects; and bootstrap inference for quantiles can be unreliable. Make sure this is what you intend; cdf_did() is identified for discrete outcomes.
summary(q1)

## OR with covariates, QTE
# \donttest{

q2 <- unc_qte(yname = "re78", dname = "treat", data = lalonde.psid,
              xformula = xf, est_method = "reg",
              biters = 20, probs = seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05))
#> Warning: The outcome `re78` looks discrete: 12% of observations equal 0. Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome. ## AIPW with covariates, QTT
# \donttest{

              xformula = xf, est_method = "aipw", target = "qtt",
              biters = 20, probs = seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05))
#> Warning: The outcome `re78` looks discrete: 12% of observations equal 0. Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome. With mass points, quantiles jump and effects at quantiles inside a mass point are 0 by construction; rank- and quantile-based identification (e.g. change-in-changes) then only bounds the effects; and bootstrap inference for quantiles can be unreliable.
